steps.text: In a small bowl, combine the eggs, raisins, and vanilla. Cover and chill for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

In a medium bowl, cream together the butter, brown sugar, and white sugar. In a separate bowl, combine the flour, salt, cinnamon and baking soda; add to the creamed mixture and stir until all of the dry ingredients are absorbed. Next, stir in the egg and raisin mixture, then stir in the rolled oats and pecans. Dough will be stiff. Drop by teaspoonfuls onto an unprepared cookie sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven, until the edges are golden. Allow cookies to cool 5 minutes on the baking sheet before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Chewy oatmeal raisin cookies with lots of flavor. You can also substitute 1/2 cup of wheat germ in place of some of the oatmeal, for a different flavor.
raw_recipe.name: The Best Oatmeal Cookies

review.reviewBody: Finally! After 30 years of many different oatmeal cookie recipes, I have hit upon one my husband really loves! Oatmeal cookies have never been his favorite because he likes chewy--not cakelike, not crispy--CHEWY cookies! He tentatively took one bite, then another and then started exclaiming, "These are really good! Wow! These are sooo good!" They are easy to make (ended up with about 6 doz.), freeze very well, and above all, THEY ARE CHEWY!!

I toasted my pecans before I added them. It gives a nice warm flavor. I used the PreHeat time as I spread the broken pecans to a baking sheet, set in the middle rack. For this step I watch and smell the pecans. 1-2 mins is all they need. Removed and cooled before adding them to the oatmeal batter.

The cookies were great! I made them as a way to use up some dried blueberries I had been given a few years ago. The soaking really made all the difference. I found that the bottoms burned a bit in my oven if I cooked them as prescribed, so I wound up having to turn off the oven about two thirds of the way through each batch, then letting them go an extra minute or two to make up for any lost heat. Doing that, the bottoms turned out golden and crispy still with a toffee-esque taste without any blackened burnt tasting bits.

This is the best oatmeal cookie recipe I've tried. They are delicious. Only change I made was to add about 1/4 t of ground nutmeg, and used walnuts, probably more than they called for. I did change the mixing method: soaked raisins in boiling water for awhile, then drained then and dried off excess water. Creamed the eggs with the butter, et al, then followed the instructions. Wow! These cookies are great. Plannied on using them for a quick breakfast on the go, but they're so good u just keep eating.

LOVE this recipe! I bake & sell thousands of cookies every year, and I have NEVER found an Oatmeal cookie recipe I liked. This is the first one that I've made several times. My tweak. I didn't soak the raisins in the egg mixture. I just assembled the recipe like I would any other cookie recipe...cream fats & sugars, add eggs & flavoring, then add dry ingredients. I think these would be good with mini CC too.

I have made these for at least 25 years but we call them Aunt Elsie's as I got the recipe from my SIL Elsie. My boys prefer them to chocolate chip. I always make the wheat germ 1/2 cup sub for oatmeal. I think the soaking of the raisins is key and use a mixer to make the dough as it mashes the raisins. They make a good emergency breakfast!

Thank you for this no fail recipe, too thin add more oats. Want it more sweet? Add more raisins. Want it crispy around the edges? Cook them longer on lower heat. Softer,? Cook less. Keep dough in the fridge and make small fresh batches every 3 or so days in the air frier. Very yummy, good late night need something cookie.

i'm a novice baker, and overbaked the first two sheets...i realized on the last few sheets thst the cookies need to be taken out when they still look a bit uncooked in the middle. Leaving them on the hot cookie sheet gives them a chance to finish cooking without being over cooked. For me it was 10 minutes at 350. Even the ones that were a bit overcooked were still delicious. Only changes i made to the recipe was to add an 1/8 tsp of cloves and allspice, and my cinnamon was a generous tsp. Saving this is a favorite for sure :)

These oatmeal cookies were chewy on the inside but crunchy around the edges. i added 1/2 tsp of cloves. My house smells amazing after baking these. I made about 19 cookies but the cooking time was about 18-20 minutes to get them golden.

I normally don't review recipes when I change them to suit my taste but this is such an excellent base recipe that I had to put in my opinion. I omitted the disgusting raisins :) and the pecans because I was going for the chewy 'little Debbie' vibe. I made oatmeal cream sandwiches with a buttercream frosting and they were loved by all!

I made these with the suggestion from another user in here to add more oats. And yes they where perfect with a 1/2 cup more oats added. Simply the best oatmeal cookies I’ve ever had. Wonderful. I added some chocolate chips. 1/3 cup and it gave the last yumminess. Try them. .
I made mine quite large and baked for the full 12 minutes. Yummy, chewy, buttery goodness!
Thin, tasteless cookies. Made sure I followed the ingredients and directions and missed no steps. Was making these for the Troops overseas, now I wasted all the ingredients. What a disappointment.
These cookies are genuinely the best oatmeals cookies I have ever eaten, definitely a keeper. No need to make changes.
I goofed up and used b. powder instead of b.soda, still came out good. Ignore the part about "drop by teaspoonfuls" - do you know how small a teaspoon is? Just use an average spoon.
The best oatmeal raisin cookie I've ever had.

these were really good! but the baking time is off. I would reccomend putting them in for about 16 minutes. also it could've used chocolate chips, white or brown would've worked. thanks! also not as chew y as people make it seem .

They're not kidding when they say these are the BEST oatmeal cookies. I am terrible at baking, but I managed to make these perfectly. I did have to add another egg to the dough because it was too dry, but that might be the difference between large and extra large eggs. I used large, so maybe thats why that happened. I also added mini chcolate chips, which was a nice touch. Lastly, I used vegetable shortening instead of butter. Chewy and crispy and not too sweet...perfection!
VERY GOOD COOKIES!!!
I followed all tge instructions exact and they came out thick and chunky and crispy... not chewy at all
